result.topic_en: The end of a fragment tabulating solutions (p,q,r,s) for which the product of two areas is a square, an editors' note on its provenance, and fragment 61, a theorem reducing the squaring of $aax^4+bxxyy+ccy^4$ to a product of four simple factors equal to a square.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 227
Si ambarum arearum productum $AB$ debeat esse quadratum, tantum sumi oportet pro numeris $a$ et $b$ quadrata; sit igitur $a=4$ et $b=1$ eruntque solutiones
\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c}
 & $p$ & $q$ & $r$ & $s$ \\
$\alpha$ & 7 & 5 & 5 & 2 \\
$\alpha$ & 12 & 2 & 7 & 3 \\
$\beta$ & \{9 & 3 & 6 & 3\} \\
 & \{3 & 1 & 2 & 1\} \\
$\beta$ & 4 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\
$\gamma$ & 24 & 7 & 17 & 14 \\
$\gamma$ & 31 & 17 & 31 & 3 \\
$\delta$ & \{24 & 9 & 18 & 15\} \\
 & \{8 & 3 & 6 & 5\} \\
$\delta$ & 11 & 5 & 11 & 1
\end{tabular}
A. m. T. I. p. 296—298.
Nota Editorum. Huic praecedenti fragmento in Adversariorum Tomo I Patris manu inscriptum est: «Omnia haec jam redacta» (Dieses ist schon ausgeführt); cum tamen in nullo cognitorum Euleri operum has investigationes detegere nobis contigerit, quae hanc ob rem et in recentissima editione Commentationum arithmeticar. desunt, esse utique potest eas in quapiam rarissima seu oblita collectione typis expressas reperiri. Hic saltem sufficiet remittere lectorem ad commentationem, cujus fragmentum supra in pag. 101 hujusce tomi Opp. posthum. reperitur, et in qua idem fere, aut simile argumentum tractatum fuisse videtur.

61.
Theorema. Haec formula $aax^4+bxxyy+ccy^4$, quadrato aequanda, semper reduci potest ad productum quatuor factoribus simplicibus constans, pariter quadrato aequandum.
Demonstratio. Formula proposita aequetur huic quadrato $\left(axx+cyy.\frac{p}{q}\right)^2$, fietque
$bqqxx+ccqqyy=2acpqxx+ccppyy$, unde fit $\frac{xx}{yy}=\frac{cc(q+p)(q-p)}{q(2acp-bq)}=\Box$.
Quadratum ergo esse debet $(q+p)(q-p)q(2acp-bq)$. Simili modo, si radicem illius formulae posuissemus
$cyy+axx.\frac{r}{s}$, prodiisset $\frac{xx}{yy}=\frac{s(2acr-bs)}{aa(s+r)(s-r)}$;
quadratum ergo debet esse $(s+r)(s-r)s(2acr-bs)$. Deinde, quia per utramque positionem est
$axx+cyy.\frac{p}{q}=cyy+axx.\frac{r}{s}$, erit $\frac{xx}{yy}=\frac{cs(q-p)}{aq(s-r)}$,
ideoque debet esse $cs(q-p).aq(s-r)=\Box$.
Corollarium. Pro $\frac{xx}{yy}$ nacti sumus sequentes tres valores:
$\frac{cc(q+p)(q-p)}{q(2acp-bq)}$, $\frac{s(2acr-bs)}{aa(s+r)(s-r)}$, $\frac{cs(q-p)}{aq(s-r)}$,
ex quorum comparatione relatio inter rationes $r:s$ et $p:q$ deduci potest. Erit enim
$r:s=\left(1+\frac{b}{ac}\right)q-p:q+p$; vel erit etiam $p:q=\left(1+\frac{b}{ac}\right)s-r:s+r$.
A. m. T. III. p. 136.

methods.what: Set the quartic equal to the square of $axx+cyy\cdot p/q$, giving x²/y² as a rational expression that must be a square
Reduction to a four-factor product required to be a square
Alternative root $cyy+axx\cdot r/s$ giving a second four-factor condition
Equating the two parametrised roots gives a third condition
Relation between the parameter ratios r:s and p:q

items.quote: Haec formula $aax^4+bxxyy+ccy^4$, quadrato aequanda, semper reduci potest ad productum quatuor factoribus simplicibus constans, pariter quadrato aequandum.
items.english: This formula $aax^4+bxxyy+ccy^4$, to be made equal to a square, can always be reduced to a product of four simple factors, likewise to be made equal to a square.
